dft.title: Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT)

fns.title: Supported special functions
fns.intro: Beyond standard trigonometric and hyperbolic functions, the calculator recognises these signal-analysis functions in symbolic input, numeric evaluation and Fourier transforms.

u.name: Unit step
u.def: Equals 1 for t ≥ 0 and 0 for t < 0. Models the abrupt switch-on of a signal: multiply by u(t) to activate a function from t = 0, or by u(t − a) to delay it to t = a.

sgn.name: Sign function
sgn.def: Returns +1 for t > 0, −1 for t < 0 and 0 at the origin. Related to the step by sgn(t) = 2u(t) − 1. Appears in the Hilbert transform and in the analysis of causal signals.

delta.name: Dirac delta
delta.def: A unit-area distribution concentrated at t = 0. Sifting property: ∫ f(t) δ(t − a) dt = f(a). Identity element of convolution and the cornerstone of LTI system theory.

rect.name: Rectangular pulse
rect.def: Equals 1 for |t| < ½, ½ at the edges and 0 outside. Use rect(t/T) for a pulse of width T, or rect((t − t₀)/T) to shift it in time.

tri.name: Triangular pulse
tri.def: A pyramid of base 2 and height 1 — the normalised self-convolution of rect. Use tri(t/T) to scale the base to 2T. Its transform is sinc², making it useful for spectral window design.

sinc.name: Sinc function
sinc.def: Defined as sin(t)/t (unnormalised sinc). Arises naturally as the transform of rect and as the frequency response of the ideal low-pass filter. By continuity, sinc(0) = 1.
